Thanks for the call earlier today — good overview. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can scope a pilot:

- Goal: integrate LLM into our internal support triage and short-response generation. Latency target: p95 < 400ms for 256-token requests.
- Volume: steady-state ~20 TPS at peak during business hours, spiky bursts up to ~50 TPS.
- Data sensitivity: customer data, must be encrypted in transit; SOC 2 + audit logs are must-haves.

Can you share: 1) recommended model variants for that latency/throughput profile, 2) any Redwood-verified benchmark links (TPS / latency percentiles) we can share with our infra team, and 3) example prompt sets you recommend for triage tasks?

Also looping in our procurement contact Daniel for next steps on contracting.

Thanks,
Sophie Chen

Hi Sophie — great to meet you today. Quick follow-up and attached items.

Recommended model variants (based on the latency & throughput targets you mentioned):
- Redwood-7B-8bit (recommended starting point): best balance of cost and p50 latency; typical throughput ~30 TPS on a 2xA10 pool.
- Redwood-13B-quant (8-bit + KV cache optimizations): stronger quality at slightly higher latency; expected p95 ~380ms for 256 tokens in our verified runs.
- Redwood-3B-fast (low-latency option): if you prioritize p95 < 250ms but can accept lower quality on long-context outputs.

Redwood-verified performance profiles (public links below) include: TPS at different batch sizes, p50/p95 latency percentiles, and memory/CPU footprints. Short highlights from the Lumen AI run we prepared:
- Redwood-7B-8bit: peak sustained TPS 28, p50 85ms, p95 320ms (256 tokens).
- Redwood-13B-quant: peak sustained TPS 14, p50 120ms, p95 380ms (256 tokens).
- Redwood-3B-fast: peak sustained TPS 60, p50 45ms, p95 210ms (256 tokens).

I've uploaded the detailed CSV of the benchmark runs (redwood-bench-tps-20260312.csv) and a short README to the perf dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/lumenai-20260312

Prompt sets: we trialed a basic triage prompt set and included a sample in the attachments (lumen-prompt-set-v1.txt). Marissa (cc'd) will add notes on prompt engineering and quality/regression checks.

Next suggested steps:
1) Quick SRE sync to validate capacity planning (we can do a 30-min deep dive next week).
2) Pilot: 2-week pilot on Dedicated (reserved pool) with nightly evals against your priority prompts.
3) Procurement: if pilot looks good, move to a 6-12 month reserved capacity commit (Marissa / I can coordinate).

Happy to set up the SRE sync — what times work for Daniel / your infra team?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Direct: (510) 555-0142

Thanks for sharing, Jordan — adding a few notes on quality and evals from the solutions side.

- Prompt set considerations: the attached lumen-prompt-set-v1 includes canonical triage prompts and a few longer-response cases. For fairness in regressions, we recommend a 200-example eval set covering intent recognition, response appropriateness, and hallucination checks.
- Regression concerns: when moving from 7B -> 13B quant variants, quality generally improves for nuance but we sometimes see new hallucination modes with factual prompts. We'll run nightly diff-evals during the pilot and surface any regressions with example prompts.
- Monitoring: we suggest enabling the per-route quality monitors in Redwood Console (thresholds, alerting on metric drift) and keeping token-level cost sampling enabled so you can correlate cost vs quality.

I also left inline comments in the benchmark CSV (attached) for a few outlier runs we saw at batch size 64.

If you can share a small sample (50-200) of anonymized user examples, we can pre-run a quality baseline and include that in the pilot metrics report.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
